description: src/error.rs:12 (`Http(reqwest::Error)`) and :97 (`WebSocket(tungstenite::Error)`) embed third-party error types directly. The doc comments correctly warn this is a semver hazard: any caller matching the inner reqwest::Error or tungstenite::Error is locked to the same major version this crate uses. The note says 'pre-1.0 limitation' but the crate is at 0.1.1 and intends to publish. RustCrypto convention and most well-maintained Rust libraries either: (a) wrap third-party errors in #[non_exhaustive] private variants with only a Display impl, hiding the inner type, (b) re-export the crate's error type so callers can match without a separate dep on reqwest/tungstenite. Right now downstream crates (jmap-mail-client, jmap-chat-client) that surface ClientError to their users also leak reqwest. The fix is non-trivial and the impact is real once 1.0 ships. Note: locked crate.
title: ClientError variants Http and WebSocket leak third-party error types in public API
